strings.text: Country Day’s Educational Resource Program “assists students in grades junior kindergarten through grade 12,” with one-on-one learning support in the Lower and Middle Schools, academic coaching in the Upper School, and accommodations for students with a documented disability.
strings.t: Educational Resource Program Country Day a “ede elèv depi junior kindergarten rive nan 12yèm ane”, ak sipò aprantisaj youn-a-youn nan Lower School ak Middle School, coaching akademik nan Upper School, ak akomodasyon pou elèv ki gen yon andikap ki dokimante.

strings.text: Sessions are billed to the student’s account: $82 for 45 minutes in the Lower School, $85 a session in the Middle and Upper Schools.
strings.t: Yo fakture sesyon yo sou kont elèv la: $82 pou 45 minit nan Lower School, $85 pou chak sesyon nan Middle School ak Upper School.

strings.text: a 45-minute Lower School session
strings.t: yon sesyon 45 minit nan Lower School

strings.text: grades JK–4, billed through the student’s account by the Business Office
strings.t: klas JK–4, Business Office la fakture l sou kont elèv la

strings.text: a Middle or Upper School session
strings.t: yon sesyon nan Middle School oswa Upper School

strings.text: Middle School learning support and Upper School academic coaching; the session length is not stated
strings.t: sipò aprantisaj nan Middle School ak coaching akademik nan Upper School; yo pa di konbyen tan yon sesyon dire

strings.text: Educational Resource Program staff
strings.t: anplwaye Educational Resource Program

strings.text: three division directors, 19 learning specialists and four academic coaches
strings.t: twa direktè divizyon, diznèf espesyalis aprantisaj ak kat coach akademik

strings.text: school counselors
strings.t: konseye lekòl

strings.text: two in each division, alongside a Director of Health and Wellness
strings.t: de nan chak divizyon, ansanm ak yon Direktè Sante ak Byennèt

strings.text: Country Day gives school-based accommodations to students with a documented disability, from its own approved list. Learning-support sessions need no testing.
strings.t: Country Day bay elèv ki gen yon andikap ki dokimante akomodasyon lekòl, ki soti nan pwòp lis apwouve li. Sesyon sipò aprantisaj yo pa bezwen okenn tès.

strings.text: Accommodations are for “students with documented disabilities,” and “A licensed service provider must document disabilities through a full psychoeducational evaluation.” Learning-support sessions are different: in the Lower School “A psychoeducational evaluation is not required for services,” and Middle School support is open to students “both with and without formal testing.”
strings.t: Akomodasyon yo se pou “elèv ki gen andikap ki dokimante”, epi “yon founisè sèvis ki gen lisans dwe dokimante andikap yo atravè yon evalyasyon psikoedikatif konplè”. Sesyon sipò aprantisaj yo diferan: nan Lower School “yo pa egzije yon evalyasyon psikoedikatif pou sèvis yo”, epi sipò Middle School la louvri pou elèv “ki gen tès fòmèl kou sa ki pa genyen”.

strings.text: The school’s pages do not mention 504 plans or IEPs. A full psychoeducational evaluation is the only evaluation accepted for formal accommodations: “A simple doctor’s note or medical diagnosis (e.g., ADHD or anxiety) does not provide enough information to justify accommodations.” Supports an outside provider suggests “are considered recommendations and are not mandated.”
strings.t: Paj lekòl la pa mansyone plan 504 ni IEP. Yon evalyasyon psikoedikatif konplè se sèl evalyasyon yo aksepte pou akomodasyon fòmèl: “Yon senp nòt doktè oswa yon dyagnostik medikal (pa egzanp, ADHD oswa enkyetid) pa bay ase enfòmasyon pou jistifye akomodasyon.” Sipò yon founisè deyò sijere “konsidere kòm rekòmandasyon epi yo pa obligatwa”.

strings.text: “Students are eligible only for Country Day-approved accommodations; accommodations outside this list are not granted.” The approved list covers classroom accommodations, Country Day tests and standardized-test requests.
strings.t: “Elèv yo kalifye sèlman pou akomodasyon Country Day apwouve; yo pa bay akomodasyon ki pa sou lis sa a.” Lis apwouve a kouvri akomodasyon nan klas, tès Country Day ak demann pou tès estanda.

strings.text: A speech-language, occupational therapy or auditory processing evaluation “may receive school approved accommodations for one year.”
strings.t: Yon evalyasyon lapawòl ak langaj, terapi okipasyonèl oswa tretman oditif “ka resevwa akomodasyon lekòl la apwouve pou yon ane”.

strings.text: Every service the school’s pages describe, grouped and coded by who delivers it. Learning-support sessions and coaching are billed per session; speech and occupational therapy come from independent providers on campus. Pick your child’s need to see what applies.
strings.t: Chak sèvis paj lekòl la dekri, gwoupe epi kode selon kiyès ki bay li. Yo fakture sesyon sipò aprantisaj ak coaching pa sesyon; terapi lapawòl ak terapi okipasyonèl soti nan founisè endepandan sou kanpis la. Chwazi bezwen pitit ou a pou wè sa ki aplike.

strings.text: One-on-one Orton-Gillingham-based support in the Lower School, and small reading groups in K–1.
strings.t: Sipò youn-a-youn ki baze sou Orton-Gillingham nan Lower School, ak ti gwoup lekti nan K–1.

strings.text: Lower School specialists “bring advanced training, including Orton-Gillingham,” and the Hochman Method (The Writing Revolution). “For K–1 students, the Reading Specialist provides small-group literacy instruction.”
strings.t: Espesyalis Lower School yo “pote fòmasyon avanse, tankou Orton-Gillingham”, ak Hochman Method (The Writing Revolution). “Pou elèv K–1, Reading Specialist la bay ansèyman lekti ak ekriti an ti gwoup.”

strings.text: Academic coaching in the Upper School, and executive-skills support in the Middle School.
strings.t: Coaching akademik nan Upper School, ak sipò pou konpetans egzekitif nan Middle School.

strings.text: Each coaching session “uses a student’s current coursework as the practice ground.” Upper School coaching is scheduled “on a first-come, first-served basis” and “begins after the first day of school as staffing allows.”
strings.t: Chak sesyon coaching “sèvi ak kou elèv la ap suiv kounye a kòm teren pratik”. Yo pwograme coaching Upper School “selon premye ki vini, premye ki sèvi” epi li “kòmanse apre premye jou lekòl la selon anplwaye ki disponib”.

strings.text: One-on-one multi-sensory math in the Lower School, and math support in the Middle School.
strings.t: Matematik milti-sansoryèl youn-a-youn nan Lower School, ak sipò matematik nan Middle School.

strings.text: Lower School math is taught with “hands-on manipulatives, explicit language and multi-sensory engagement.” Middle School specialists help students strengthen “writing, math, and reading comprehension within the context of their coursework.”
strings.t: Nan Lower School, yo anseye matematik ak “materyèl pou manipile, langaj klè ak angajman milti-sansoryèl”. Espesyalis Middle School yo ede elèv yo ranfòse “ekriti, matematik ak konpreyansyon lekti nan kontèks kou yo”.

strings.text: Screening and therapy on campus, through an independent provider the family pays directly.
strings.t: Depistaj ak terapi sou kanpis la, atravè yon founisè endepandan fanmi an peye dirèkteman.

strings.text: TerrificTalkers’ speech-language pathologists screen on campus for $25.00 and “operate independently of this school and are not employees of the school.” Therapy is arranged and paid for with the provider.
strings.t: Patolojis lapawòl ak langaj TerrificTalkers yo fè depistaj sou kanpis la pou $25.00 epi yo “travay endepandan de lekòl sa a epi yo pa anplwaye lekòl la”. Yo fè aranjman pou terapi a epi peye l ak founisè a.

strings.text: Occupational therapy on campus through an independent provider. No physical therapy is listed.
strings.t: Terapi okipasyonèl sou kanpis la atravè yon founisè endepandan. Yo pa mansyone fizyoterapi.

strings.text: Southern Piedmont Pediatric Therapy screens for $25, and “OT’s are on campus 1-2 days per week.” If you schedule therapy, “all financial arrangements will be between you and Southern Piedmont Pediatric Therapy.”
strings.t: Southern Piedmont Pediatric Therapy fè depistaj pou $25, epi “terapis okipasyonèl yo sou kanpis la 1-2 jou pa semèn”. Si ou pwograme terapi, “tout aranjman finansye ap fèt ant ou menm ak Southern Piedmont Pediatric Therapy”.

strings.text: Six school counselors, two in each division, and published crisis lines.
strings.t: Sis konseye lekòl, de nan chak divizyon, ak liy kriz ki pibliye.

strings.text: Lower School counselors provide “short-term individual and/or family counseling if needed, and referral to outside experts when appropriate.” The Health Services page links 988, the Crisis Text Line and the NC Peer Warmline.
strings.t: Konseye Lower School yo bay “konsèy endividyèl ak/oswa fanmi pou yon ti tan si sa nesesè, ak referans bay ekspè deyò lè sa apwopriye”. Paj Health Services la gen lyen pou 988, Crisis Text Line ak NC Peer Warmline.

strings.text: No gifted or advanced-learner program is described.
strings.t: Yo pa dekri okenn pwogram pou elèv ki gen don oswa ki avanse.

strings.text: The school’s learning-support pages describe no gifted program. Ask what is available for advanced learners.
strings.t: Paj sipò aprantisaj lekòl la pa dekri okenn pwogram pou elèv ki gen don. Mande kisa ki disponib pou elèv ki avanse.

strings.text: Learning & academic support
strings.t: Sipò pou aprantisaj ak etid

strings.text: Specialized teachers
strings.t: Pwofesè espesyalize

strings.text: Nineteen learning specialists and four Upper School academic coaches, led by a director in each division, plus a Lower School Reading Specialist and Literacy Coach. Lower School specialists “bring advanced training, including Orton-Gillingham.”
strings.t: Diznèf espesyalis aprantisaj ak kat coach akademik Upper School, yon direktè nan chak divizyon dirije yo, plis yon Reading Specialist ak Literacy Coach nan Lower School. Espesyalis Lower School yo “pote fòmasyon avanse, tankou Orton-Gillingham”.

strings.text: Reading intervention
strings.t: Entèvansyon nan lekti

strings.text: Lower School specialists give one-on-one support in reading and writing, “typically twice per week,” drawing on Orton-Gillingham and the Hochman Method. K–1 students may also get “small-group literacy instruction” from the Reading Specialist; the school does not say whether those groups are billed.
strings.t: Espesyalis Lower School yo bay sipò youn-a-youn nan lekti ak ekriti, “anjeneral de fwa pa semèn”, ki baze sou Orton-Gillingham ak Hochman Method. Elèv K–1 ka resevwa tou “ansèyman lekti ak ekriti an ti gwoup” nan men Reading Specialist la; lekòl la pa di si yo fakture gwoup sa yo.

strings.text: Math intervention
strings.t: Entèvansyon nan matematik

strings.text: One-on-one “Multi-Sensory Math” in the Lower School, and math within Middle School learning support.
strings.t: “Matematik milti-sansoryèl” youn-a-youn nan Lower School, ak matematik nan sipò aprantisaj Middle School.

strings.text: 1:1 / small-group instruction
strings.t: Ansèyman 1:1 / an ti gwoup

strings.text: One-on-one in every division: Lower School sessions are “$82 per 45-minute session,” Middle School sessions “$85 per session.” Small groups are for K–1 literacy only.
strings.t: Youn-a-youn nan chak divizyon: sesyon Lower School yo se “$82 pou chak sesyon 45 minit”, sesyon Middle School yo “$85 pou chak sesyon”. Ti gwoup yo se sèlman pou lekti ak ekriti nan K–1.

strings.text: Executive-function coaching
strings.t: Coaching pou fonksyon egzekitif

strings.text: Upper School academic coaching is “billed at $85 per session”: one coach across core classes in 9th grade, then Humanities or STEM coaching in grades 10–12. Middle School support covers “Executive skills (organization, planning, study routines).”
strings.t: Coaching akademik Upper School la “fakture a $85 pou chak sesyon”: yon coach pou kou prensipal yo nan 9yèm ane, apre sa coaching nan Imanite oswa STEM nan klas 10–12. Sipò Middle School la kouvri “Konpetans egzekitif (òganizasyon, planifikasyon, abitid etid)”.

strings.text: Learning-support class
strings.t: Kou sipò aprantisaj

strings.text: No learning-support class is offered, but sessions “are a permanent part of student schedules” and are “treated as class periods,” held during study halls, special-area classes or lunch.
strings.t: Pa gen klas sipò aprantisaj, men sesyon yo “se yon pati pèmanan nan orè elèv yo” epi yo “trete yo kòm peryòd klas”, pandan sal etid, klas espesyal oswa manje midi.

strings.text: Accommodations & learning plan
strings.t: Akomodasyon ak plan aprantisaj

strings.text: Accommodations come only from the school’s approved list and are recorded in a “Confidential Academic Plan (CAP)” that every teacher can see. Middle and Upper School students with “a documented mental health diagnosis may receive temporary accommodations” while awaiting an evaluation.
strings.t: Akomodasyon yo soti sèlman nan lis lekòl la apwouve epi yo anrejistre yo nan yon “Confidential Academic Plan (CAP)” tout pwofesè ka wè. Elèv Middle School ak Upper School ki gen “yon dyagnostik sante mantal ki dokimante ka resevwa akomodasyon tanporè” pandan y ap tann yon evalyasyon.

strings.text: Specially designed instruction
strings.t: Ansèyman ki fèt espesyalman

strings.text: Not described. The school says accommodations change “how a student accesses learning—not what they are expected to learn.”
strings.t: Yo pa dekri l. Lekòl la di akomodasyon yo chanje “fason yon elèv jwenn aksè ak aprantisaj la, pa sa yo atann li aprann”.

strings.text: Self-contained / separate program
strings.t: Pwogram apa / klas separe

strings.text: No separate program described.
strings.t: Yo pa dekri okenn pwogram apa.

strings.text: Gifted / advanced
strings.t: Elèv ki gen don / nivo avanse

strings.text: Eligibility documentation
strings.t: Dokiman pou kalifye

strings.text: Formal accommodations need a full psychoeducational evaluation, reviewed every three years in Lower and Middle School and every four in Upper School, and submitted through the ERP’s secure online form. Learning-support sessions need none.
strings.t: Akomodasyon fòmèl yo bezwen yon evalyasyon psikoedikatif konplè, yo revize chak twa an nan Lower School ak Middle School epi chak kat an nan Upper School, epi yo soumèt li atravè fòm an liy sekirize ERP a. Sesyon sipò aprantisaj yo pa bezwen youn.

strings.text: Therapy & related services
strings.t: Terapi ak sèvis ki gen rapò

strings.text: Speech-language therapy
strings.t: Terapi pou pale ak langaj

strings.text: TerrificTalkers screens on campus for $25.00 and can provide therapy at school; the family pays the provider directly. The school calls them “contracted” therapists “who provide additional services during the school day.”
strings.t: TerrificTalkers fè depistaj sou kanpis la pou $25.00 epi li ka bay terapi lekòl la; fanmi an peye founisè a dirèkteman. Lekòl la rele yo terapis “sou kontra” “ki bay sèvis anplis pandan jounen lekòl la”.

strings.text: Occupational therapy
strings.t: Terapi okipasyonèl

strings.text: Southern Piedmont Pediatric Therapy screens for $25 and is “on campus 1-2 days per week”; therapy is arranged and paid for with the provider.
strings.t: Southern Piedmont Pediatric Therapy fè depistaj pou $25 epi li “sou kanpis la 1-2 jou pa semèn”; yo fè aranjman pou terapi a epi peye l ak founisè a.

strings.text: Physical therapy
strings.t: Fizyoterapi

strings.text: Not listed by the school.
strings.t: Lekòl la pa mansyone l.

strings.text: Assessment
strings.t: Evalyasyon

strings.text: Early identification (JK–2)
strings.t: Idantifikasyon bonè (JK–2)

strings.text: Lower School students are identified through “benchmark assessments given at the beginning, middle, and end of the school year,” and the school offers speech-language and occupational therapy screenings.
strings.t: Yo idantifye elèv Lower School atravè “evalyasyon referans yo bay nan kòmansman, nan mitan ak nan fen ane lekòl la”, epi lekòl la ofri depistaj lapawòl ak langaj ak terapi okipasyonèl.

strings.text: Testing accommodations
strings.t: Aranjman pou tès

strings.text: Approved accommodations include “Extended time (50% more)” on Country Day tests. The ERP submits College Board, ACT and IB requests, but “Country Day accommodations do not automatically transfer.”
strings.t: Akomodasyon apwouve yo gen ladan “Tan anplis (50% plis)” nan tès Country Day. ERP a soumèt demann bay College Board, ACT ak IB, men “akomodasyon Country Day yo pa transfere otomatikman”.

strings.text: Entrance testing
strings.t: Tès antre

strings.text: A psychologist’s standardized screening for younger applicants, the ISEE for grades 5–12, and the TOEFL for international applicants.
strings.t: Yon depistaj estanda yon sikològ fè pou pi piti kandida yo, ISEE pou klas 5–12, ak TOEFL pou kandida entènasyonal yo.

strings.text: Psychoeducational evaluation
strings.t: Evalyasyon psikoedikasyonèl

strings.text: Done by outside providers at the family’s cost. The school publishes a list of preferred providers, updated January 2026, some accepting insurance, and “financial aid options are available for qualifying families.”
strings.t: Founisè deyò fè l, fanmi an peye. Lekòl la pibliye yon lis founisè li prefere, mete ajou janvye 2026, kèk ladan yo aksepte asirans, epi “gen opsyon èd finansye pou fanmi ki kalifye”.

strings.text: Wellness & health
strings.t: Byennèt ak sante

strings.text: Counseling & emotional support
strings.t: Konsèy ak sipò emosyonèl

strings.text: Six school counselors, two in each division; three hold the title Director of Counseling. Lower School counselors provide “short-term individual and/or family counseling if needed, and referral to outside experts when appropriate.”
strings.t: Sis konseye lekòl, de nan chak divizyon; twa gen tit Direktè Konsèy. Konseye Lower School yo bay “konsèy endividyèl ak/oswa fanmi pou yon ti tan si sa nesesè, ak referans bay ekspè deyò lè sa apwopriye”.

strings.text: Emotional & behavioral intervention
strings.t: Entèvansyon pou emosyon ak konpòtman

strings.text: No program is described beyond short-term counseling and referral.
strings.t: Yo pa dekri okenn pwogram pi lwen pase konsèy pou yon ti tan ak referans.

strings.text: Crisis resources
strings.t: Resous pou kriz

strings.text: The Health Services page links Crisis Service Lines: the 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline, the Crisis Text Line (text HOME to 741741) and the NC Peer Warmline (1-855-733-7762).
strings.t: Paj Health Services la gen lyen pou liy kriz: 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline, Crisis Text Line (voye HOME nan 741741) ak NC Peer Warmline (1-855-733-7762).

strings.text: School psychologist
strings.t: Sikològ lekòl

strings.text: None named. The Director of Health and Wellness, who started July 1, 2026, is “A licensed clinical psychologist.”
strings.t: Yo pa nonmen okenn. Direktè Sante ak Byennèt la, ki te kòmanse 1ye jiyè 2026, se “Yon sikològ klinik ki gen lisans”.

strings.text: School nurse
strings.t: Enfimyè lekòl

strings.text: “Two full-time nurses on each campus.”
strings.t: “De enfimyè aplentan sou chak kanpis.”

strings.text: Language
strings.t: Lang

strings.text: ESL / English-language support
strings.t: ESL / sipò nan angle

strings.text: The school has “a full-time English as a Second Language program,” and the directory lists an English and ESL Teacher in the Upper School.
strings.t: Lekòl la gen “yon pwogram aplentan Anglè kòm Dezyèm Lang”, epi anyè a mansyone yon Pwofesè Anglè ak ESL nan Upper School.

strings.text: Speech and occupational therapy are available on campus during the school day from independent providers, arranged and paid for directly by the family. Physical therapy is not listed.
strings.t: Terapi lapawòl ak terapi okipasyonèl disponib sou kanpis la pandan jounen lekòl la atravè founisè endepandan, fanmi an fè aranjman epi peye dirèkteman. Yo pa mansyone fizyoterapi.

strings.text: Speech-language
strings.t: Pale ak langaj

strings.text: TerrificTalkers, on campus. Screening $25.00; therapy fees are set by the provider.
strings.t: TerrificTalkers, sou kanpis la. Depistaj $25.00; founisè a fikse pri terapi a.

strings.text: Occupational
strings.t: Okipasyonèl

strings.text: Southern Piedmont Pediatric Therapy, on campus 1–2 days a week. Screening $25; therapy fees are set by the provider.
strings.t: Southern Piedmont Pediatric Therapy, sou kanpis la 1–2 jou pa semèn. Depistaj $25; founisè a fikse pri terapi a.

strings.text: Physical
strings.t: Fizik

strings.text: Both providers “operate independently” of the school. Screening forms go home through the Lower School; the school does not say whether screening is offered in the Middle or Upper School.
strings.t: Toude founisè yo “travay endepandan” de lekòl la. Fòm depistaj yo ale lakay atravè Lower School; lekòl la pa di si yo ofri depistaj nan Middle School oswa Upper School.

strings.text: Lower School students are screened three times a year, and the Educational Resource Program tiers support from the results. Formal accommodations need a full psychoeducational evaluation from an outside provider.
strings.t: Yo fè depistaj pou elèv Lower School twa fwa pa ane, epi Educational Resource Program la òganize sipò an nivo selon rezilta yo. Akomodasyon fòmèl yo bezwen yon evalyasyon psikoedikatif konplè yon founisè deyò fè.

strings.text: Benchmark screening (K–4)
strings.t: Depistaj referans (K–4)

strings.text: “Students are identified for support based on benchmark assessments given at the beginning, middle, and end of the school year.”
strings.t: “Yo idantifye elèv pou sipò selon evalyasyon referans yo bay nan kòmansman, nan mitan ak nan fen ane lekòl la.”

strings.text: Data analysis meetings with the Literacy Leadership Team decide which of three tiers of support fits: classroom strategies, K–1 small groups, or one-on-one sessions.
strings.t: Reyinyon analiz done ak Literacy Leadership Team la deside kiyès nan twa nivo sipò yo ki bon: estrateji nan klas, ti gwoup K–1, oswa sesyon youn-a-youn.

strings.text: Educational screening
strings.t: Depistaj edikatif

strings.text: With a parent’s signed consent, the school does “an educational screening” to “identify individual educational needs in order to aid in individualizing instruction.”
strings.t: Avèk konsantman siyen yon paran, lekòl la fè “yon depistaj edikatif” pou “idantifye bezwen edikatif endividyèl yo pou ede adapte ansèyman an pou chak elèv”.

strings.text: Speech-language and occupational therapy screening
strings.t: Depistaj lapawòl ak langaj ak terapi okipasyonèl

strings.text: Independent providers screen on campus for $25. OT screenings are “brief 15-20 minute clinical observations to determine if an OT evaluation is needed”; the speech screening “does not serve as a comprehensive speech/language evaluation.”
strings.t: Founisè endepandan fè depistaj sou kanpis la pou $25. Depistaj terapi okipasyonèl yo se “kout obsèvasyon klinik 15-20 minit pou detèmine si yon evalyasyon terapi okipasyonèl nesesè”; depistaj lapawòl la “pa sèvi kòm yon evalyasyon lapawòl/langaj konplè”.

strings.text: “A licensed service provider must document disabilities through a full psychoeducational evaluation,” at the family’s cost. The school publishes a preferred-provider list, updated January 2026.
strings.t: “Yon founisè sèvis ki gen lisans dwe dokimante andikap yo atravè yon evalyasyon psikoedikatif konplè”, fanmi an peye. Lekòl la pibliye yon lis founisè li prefere, mete ajou janvye 2026.

strings.text: The accommodations page says evaluations are reviewed every three years in Lower and Middle School and every four in Upper School; the linked policy says three years through grade 5 and four from grade 6.
strings.t: Paj akomodasyon an di yo revize evalyasyon yo chak twa an nan Lower School ak Middle School epi chak kat an nan Upper School; règleman ki lye a di twa an jiska klas 5 ak kat an apati klas 6.

strings.text: Confidential Academic Plan
strings.t: Confidential Academic Plan

strings.text: “Teachers and Learning Support staff review each student’s psychoeducational profile and recommended accommodations,” and approved accommodations go into the student’s Confidential Academic Plan (CAP).
strings.t: “Pwofesè yo ak anplwaye Learning Support revize pwofil psikoedikatif chak elèv ak akomodasyon yo rekòmande”, epi akomodasyon apwouve yo antre nan Confidential Academic Plan (CAP) elèv la.

strings.text: Middle and Upper School students with a documented mental health diagnosis may get temporary accommodations through the school counselor while awaiting an evaluation.
strings.t: Elèv Middle School ak Upper School ki gen yon dyagnostik sante mantal ki dokimante ka jwenn akomodasyon tanporè atravè konseye lekòl la pandan y ap tann yon evalyasyon.

strings.text: Approved accommodations apply to “Daily coursework and quizzes” and to “Country Day-administered exams, including midterms and finals.” Standardized-test accommodations “must be approved separately by the College Board or ACT.”
strings.t: Akomodasyon apwouve yo aplike pou “Devwa chak jou ak ti egzamen” ak pou “egzamen Country Day administre, tankou egzamen mitan ane ak egzamen final”. Akomodasyon pou tès estanda “dwe apwouve apa pa College Board oswa ACT”.

strings.text: In grades 6–12, testing must reach the school at least seven business days before reading day to be used on exams.
strings.t: Nan klas 6–12, rezilta tès yo dwe rive lekòl la omwen sèt jou ouvrab anvan jou revizyon an pou yo ka sèvi pou egzamen yo.

strings.text: Forty named staff: the 26-person Educational Resource Program, the Lower School Reading Specialist, the Director of Health and Wellness, seven counselors, four nurses and an ESL teacher.
strings.t: Karant anplwaye ki gen non: 26 moun Educational Resource Program la, Reading Specialist Lower School la, Direktè Sante ak Byennèt la, sèt konseye, kat enfimyè ak yon pwofesè ESL.

strings.t: Direktè ERP Lower School

strings.text: Learning Specialist, Lower School
strings.t: Espesyalis aprantisaj, Lower School

strings.text: Reading Specialist/Literacy Coach, Lower School
strings.t: Espesyalis lekti/Coach lekti ak ekriti, Lower School

strings.text: Director of Middle School ERP
strings.t: Direktè ERP Middle School

strings.text: Learning Specialist, Middle School
strings.t: Espesyalis aprantisaj, Middle School

strings.text: Director of Upper School ERP
strings.t: Direktè ERP Upper School

strings.text: Academic Coach, Upper School

strings.text: Thirteen questions to take on the tour, covering what the school’s site leaves unanswered or says two ways: prior plans, evaluation timing, fees, therapy, methods and staffing.
strings.t: Trèz kesyon pou pote pandan vizit la, sou sa sit lekòl la pa reponn oswa di de fason: plan anvan, delè evalyasyon, frè, terapi, metòd ak anplwaye.

strings.text: How is a 504 plan, IEP or another school’s accommodations plan treated when a student enrolls? Is a new psychoeducational evaluation always required?
strings.t: Kijan yo trete yon plan 504, yon IEP oswa plan akomodasyon yon lòt lekòl lè yon elèv enskri? Èske yo toujou egzije yon nouvo evalyasyon psikoedikatif?

strings.text: Your accommodations page says evaluations are reviewed every three years in Lower and Middle School, but the evaluation policy says three years through grade 5 and four from grade 6. Which applies to grades 5–8?
strings.t: Paj akomodasyon nou an di yo revize evalyasyon yo chak twa an nan Lower School ak Middle School, men règleman evalyasyon an di twa an jiska klas 5 ak kat an apati klas 6. Kiyès ki aplike pou klas 5–8?

strings.text: How long is a Middle School or Upper School session at $85?
strings.t: Konbyen tan yon sesyon Middle School oswa Upper School a $85 dire?

strings.text: Are the K–1 small reading groups with the Reading Specialist billed, or included in tuition?
strings.t: Èske yo fakture ti gwoup lekti K–1 ak Reading Specialist la, oswa èske yo enkli nan frè lekòl la?

strings.text: Does financial aid cover Educational Resource Program sessions or academic coaching?
strings.t: Èske èd finansye kouvri sesyon Educational Resource Program oswa coaching akademik?

strings.text: What do TerrificTalkers and Southern Piedmont Pediatric Therapy charge for therapy, and do they accept insurance?
strings.t: Konbyen TerrificTalkers ak Southern Piedmont Pediatric Therapy mande pou terapi, epi èske yo aksepte asirans?

strings.text: Are speech-language and occupational therapy screenings available in the Middle and Upper Schools?
strings.t: Èske gen depistaj lapawòl ak langaj ak terapi okipasyonèl nan Middle School ak Upper School?

strings.text: Can physical therapy take place on campus during the school day?
strings.t: Èske fizyoterapi ka fèt sou kanpis la pandan jounen lekòl la?

strings.text: Do you ever modify the curriculum, or is support always accommodations and one-on-one sessions?
strings.t: Èske nou janm modifye kourikoulòm nan, oswa èske sipò a toujou se akomodasyon ak sesyon youn-a-youn?

strings.text: What do you offer advanced or gifted learners?
strings.t: Kisa nou ofri elèv ki avanse oswa ki gen don?

strings.text: Is there a school psychologist, and how does the Director of Health and Wellness work with the Educational Resource Program?
strings.t: Èske gen yon sikològ lekòl, epi kijan Direktè Sante ak Byennèt la travay ak Educational Resource Program la?

strings.text: Upper School coaching is first-come, first-served and depends on staffing, and two academic coach positions are posted. How likely is a new student to get a coaching slot?
strings.t: Coaching Upper School la se premye ki vini, premye ki sèvi epi li depann de anplwaye ki disponib, epi gen de pòs coach akademik ki afiche. Ki chans yon nouvo elèv genyen pou l jwenn yon plas nan coaching?

strings.text: Is English-language (ESL) support offered below the Upper School, and is there a fee?
strings.t: Èske yo ofri sipò Anglè (ESL) anba Upper School, epi èske gen yon frè?

strings.text: Cannon’s Learning Support Program “helps students with diagnosed learning differences become successful learners and confident self-advocates,” with a learning specialist in each division from Junior Kindergarten through 12th grade.
strings.t: Learning Support Program Cannon an “ede elèv ki gen diferans nan fason yo aprann ki dyagnostike vin elèv ki reyisi ak moun ki gen konfyans pou defann pwòp bezwen yo”, ak yon espesyalis aprantisaj nan chak divizyon depi Junior Kindergarten rive nan 12yèm ane.

strings.text: The school publishes no fee for learning support.
strings.t: Lekòl la pa pibliye okenn frè pou sipò aprantisaj.

strings.text: Learning support is for enrolled Cannon students with a diagnosed learning difference, documented by a recent psychoeducational evaluation.
strings.t: Sipò aprantisaj la se pou elèv ki enskri nan Cannon ki gen yon diferans nan fason yo aprann ki dyagnostike, dokimante pa yon evalyasyon psikoedikasyonèl resan.

strings.text: The policy requires that the student “must be a current student enrolled at Cannon School,” that parents “complete a request for Learning Support Services,” a “history of academic difficulty,” and a learning difference “diagnosed and documented by a certified professional in a recent (last 3 years) formal psycho-educational evaluation” done “by a licensed clinical psychologist.”
strings.t: Règleman an egzije elèv la “dwe yon elèv ki enskri kounye a nan Cannon School”, paran yo “ranpli yon demann pou sèvis Learning Support”, yon “istwa difikilte akademik”, ak yon diferans nan fason elèv la aprann “ki dyagnostike epi dokimante pa yon pwofesyonèl sètifye nan yon evalyasyon psikoedikasyonèl fòmèl resan (3 dènye ane yo)” ki fèt “pa yon sikològ klinik ki gen lisans”.

strings.text: The school’s pages do not mention 504 plans or IEPs. Accommodations need documentation: “No accommodation will be provided unless a disclosure with appropriate documentation has been made to the school,” and “No official Learning Plan will be constructed without a complete psychological-educational evaluation.” The request form asks what accommodations the student has had in the past.
strings.t: Paj lekòl la pa mansyone plan 504 ni IEP. Akomodasyon yo bezwen dokiman: “Okenn akomodasyon p ap bay si yo pa fè lekòl la yon divilgasyon ak dokiman ki apwopriye”, epi “Okenn Learning Plan ofisyèl p ap fèt san yon evalyasyon psikoedikasyonèl konplè”. Fòm demann lan mande ki akomodasyon elèv la te genyen nan tan pase.

strings.text: “Acceptance of a student into Cannon School does not imply that the school will assume the responsibility for all of the special learning needs of the child, especially when such needs may require a modification/alteration of the school’s curriculum or when the child’s needs are beyond Cannon’s present resources.”
strings.t: “Lè Cannon School aksepte yon elèv, sa pa vle di lekòl la ap pran responsablite pou tout bezwen aprantisaj espesyal timoun nan, sitou lè bezwen sa yo ka mande yon modifikasyon/chanjman nan kourikoulòm lekòl la oswa lè bezwen timoun nan depase resous Cannon genyen kounye a.”

strings.text: For a hearing, speech/language or vision impairment without a full evaluation, accommodations “will be considered on a case-by-case basis.”
strings.t: Pou yon pwoblèm tande, pale/langaj oswa wè san yon evalyasyon konplè, akomodasyon yo “ap konsidere ka pa ka”.

strings.text: Every service the school’s pages describe, grouped and coded by who delivers it. Cannon publishes no fee for any of them. Pick your child’s need to see what applies.
strings.t: Chak sèvis paj lekòl la dekri, ranje an gwoup e make dapre kiyès ki bay li. Cannon pa pibliye okenn frè pou yonn nan yo. Chwazi bezwen pitit ou pou wè sa ki aplike.

strings.text: A Lower School reading interventionist and specialist-built learning plans. No reading method is named.
strings.t: Yon espesyalis entèvansyon nan lekti nan Lower School ak plan aprantisaj espesyalis yo fè. Yo pa nonmen okenn metòd lekti.

strings.text: The Reading Interventionist “may provide small-group instruction designed to close specific skill gaps.” Ask which reading approach is used, and what reading support looks like after 4th grade.
strings.t: Espesyalis entèvansyon nan lekti a “ka bay ansèyman an ti gwoup ki fèt pou ranpli twou nan konpetans espesifik”. Mande ki apwòch lekti yo itilize, ak kijan sipò lekti a ye apre 4yèm ane.

strings.text: One-on-one executive-function coaching in the Middle and Upper Schools.
strings.t: Coaching fonksyon egzekitif youn-a-youn nan Middle School ak Upper School.

strings.text: Upper School Academic Coaches work “in a relational 1:1 environment” on “planning, organization, task initiation, flexibility, attention, self-control, metacognition, and more.”
strings.t: Academic Coaches Upper School yo travay “nan yon anviwònman relasyonèl 1:1” sou “planifikasyon, òganizasyon, kòmanse travay, fleksibilite, atansyon, kontwòl tèt ou, metakognisyon, ak plis ankò”.

strings.text: Peer-led Math Lab in the Upper School. No math-specific intervention is named.
strings.t: Yon Math Lab elèv yo dirije nan Upper School. Yo pa nonmen okenn entèvansyon espesyal pou matematik.

strings.text: In the Math Lab, “Tutors and teachers partner with learners to break down challenging concepts.” The school does not describe math intervention below the Upper School.
strings.t: Nan Math Lab la, “titè ak pwofesè travay ansanm ak elèv yo pou dekoupe konsèp ki difisil yo”. Lekòl la pa dekri okenn entèvansyon nan matematik anvan Upper School.

strings.text: By referral. Plan on an outside provider.
strings.t: Pa referans. Planifye ak yon founisè deyò.

strings.text: The Lower School Learning Specialist gives “guidance for families to secure external resources, such as speech therapists or tutors.”
strings.t: Espesyalis aprantisaj Lower School la bay “konsèy pou fanmi yo jwenn resous deyò, tankou terapis lapawòl oswa titè”.

strings.text: Not published. Plan on an outside provider.
strings.t: Pa pibliye. Planifye ak yon founisè deyò.

strings.text: Neither occupational nor physical therapy appears on the school’s site.
strings.t: Ni terapi okipasyonèl ni fizyoterapi pa parèt sou sit lekòl la.

strings.text: Five counselors offer short-term counseling and refer out for longer-term therapy.
strings.t: Senk konseye ofri konsèy kout tèm epi refere pou terapi pi long tèm.

strings.text: Lower School counselors provide “short-term individual counseling sessions” and “community resource referrals (including longer-term therapy services).”
strings.t: Konseye Lower School yo bay “sesyon konsèy endividyèl kout tèm” ak “referans pou resous nan kominote a (ladan l sèvis terapi pi long tèm)”.

strings.text: Reading enrichment in the Lower School and an advanced course track in the Upper School.
strings.t: Anrichisman nan lekti nan Lower School ak yon chemen kou avanse nan Upper School.

strings.text: The Reading Interventionist “may offer targeted academic enrichment”; the Upper School offers Honors Accelerated, AP and AT courses and an Independent Study Program. No formal gifted program is described.
strings.t: Espesyalis entèvansyon nan lekti a “ka ofri anrichisman akademik ki vize”; Upper School ofri kou Honors Accelerated, AP ak AT ak yon Independent Study Program. Yo pa dekri okenn pwogram fòmèl pou elèv ki gen don.

strings.text: “A dedicated learning specialist for each of division, Lower School, Middle School, and Upper School.” Four are named, plus a Lower School Reading Interventionist.
strings.t: “Yon espesyalis aprantisaj espesyalman pou chak divizyon, Lower School, Middle School ak Upper School.” Yo nonmen kat, plis yon espesyalis entèvansyon nan lekti nan Lower School.

strings.text: Lower School small groups with the Reading Interventionist “designed to close specific skill gaps.” No method (e.g., Orton-Gillingham, structured literacy) is named.
strings.t: Ti gwoup nan Lower School ak espesyalis entèvansyon nan lekti a, “ki fèt pou ranpli twou nan konpetans espesifik”. Yo pa nonmen okenn metòd (pa egzanp, Orton-Gillingham, alfabetizasyon estriktire).

strings.text: No math-specific intervention described; the Upper School Math Lab is peer tutoring.
strings.t: Yo pa dekri okenn entèvansyon espesyal pou matematik; Math Lab Upper School la se titora ant elèv.

strings.text: Small-group reading in the Lower School; one-on-one coaching with the Middle and Upper School learning specialists.
strings.t: Lekti an ti gwoup nan Lower School; coaching youn-a-youn ak espesyalis aprantisaj Middle School ak Upper School yo.

strings.text: Academic Labs (9–12)
strings.t: Laboratwa akademik (9–12)

strings.text: “Faculty-facilitated, peer-led tutoring in writing, math, and science,” plus a World Languages Lab, “available at consistent times and locations during the school day.” In the Middle School, help from teachers: “No fee is charged.”
strings.t: “Titora ant elèv, pwofesè yo fasilite, nan ekriti, matematik ak syans”, plis yon World Languages Lab, “ki disponib nan lè ak kote ki fiks pandan jounen lekòl la”. Nan Middle School, èd pwofesè yo: “Yo pa mande okenn frè.”

strings.text: One-on-one academic coaching in the Middle School and, in the Upper School, Academic Coaches who build “executive functioning (EF) skills.”
strings.t: Coaching akademik youn-a-youn nan Middle School epi, nan Upper School, Academic Coaches ki devlope “konpetans fonksyon egzekitif (EF)”.

strings.text: No learning-support course appears in the 2026-2027 Upper School Course Catalog.
strings.t: Okenn kou sipò aprantisaj pa parèt nan katalòg kou 2026-2027 Upper School la.

strings.text: The Learning Specialist writes a Learning Plan listing classroom and testing accommodations, such as “preferential seating, note-taking assistance, extended time for tests, alternate assessment location.”
strings.t: Espesyalis aprantisaj la ekri yon Learning Plan ki bay lis akomodasyon nan klas ak pou tès, tankou “plas preferansyèl, èd pou pran nòt, plis tan pou egzamen, lòt kote pou evalyasyon”.

strings.text: Not described. The policy says acceptance does not imply responsibility for needs that “may require a modification/alteration of the school’s curriculum.”
strings.t: Pa dekri. Règleman an di admisyon pa vle di lekòl la responsab bezwen ki “ka mande yon modifikasyon/chanjman nan kourikoulòm lekòl la”.

strings.text: No separate program described; the Middle School ARC brings “neurodiverse and non-neurodiverse learners” together “side by side.”
strings.t: Yo pa dekri okenn pwogram apa; ARC Middle School la mete “elèv newodivès ak elèv ki pa newodivès” ansanm “kòt a kòt”.

strings.text: Lower School reading enrichment; Upper School Honors Accelerated, AP and AT courses and an Independent Study Program. No formal gifted program.
strings.t: Anrichisman nan lekti nan Lower School; nan Upper School, kou Honors Accelerated, AP ak AT ak yon Independent Study Program. Pa gen pwogram fòmèl pou elèv ki gen don.

strings.text: A complete psychoeducational evaluation from the last 3 years, with “test results with subtest scores (standard or scaled scores)” and recommended accommodations.
strings.t: Yon evalyasyon psikoedikasyonèl konplè ki fèt nan 3 dènye ane yo, ak “rezilta tès ak nòt pou chak sou-tès (nòt estanda oswa nòt ajiste)” ak akomodasyon yo rekòmande.

strings.text: The Lower School Learning Specialist helps families “secure external resources, such as speech therapists.”
strings.t: Espesyalis aprantisaj Lower School la ede fanmi yo “jwenn resous deyò, tankou terapis lapawòl”.

strings.text: Learning support in JK–2 “focuses on early identification and classroom-based interventions”; the Learning Specialist works with teachers “to assess student needs.”
strings.t: Sipò aprantisaj nan JK–2 “konsantre sou idantifikasyon bonè ak entèvansyon nan klas la”; espesyalis aprantisaj la travay ak pwofesè yo “pou evalye bezwen elèv yo”.

strings.text: Testing accommodations are part of each Learning Plan. Once a plan has been in place “for at least four months,” the Learning Specialist may help families request College Board and ACT accommodations.
strings.t: Akomodasyon pou tès fè pati chak Learning Plan. Lè yon plan an plas “pou omwen kat mwa”, espesyalis aprantisaj la ka ede fanmi yo mande akomodasyon College Board ak ACT.

strings.text: The admissions checklist “may include” an Entrance Evaluation and a Readiness Evaluation.
strings.t: Lis admisyon an “ka gen ladan l” yon Entrance Evaluation ak yon Readiness Evaluation.

strings.text: Families supply it, from “a licensed clinical psychologist.” The school does not say it tests in-house or name providers.
strings.t: Se fanmi yo ki bay li, nan men “yon sikològ klinik ki gen lisans”. Lekòl la pa di li fè tès anndan l, ni li pa nonmen founisè.

strings.text: Five school counselors offer wellness lessons, check-ins, “short-term individual counseling sessions” and small groups, working “in collaboration with Learning Specialists.”
strings.t: Senk konseye lekòl ofri leson sou byennèt, ti chèk-in, “sesyon konsèy endividyèl kout tèm” ak ti gwoup, yo travay “an kolaborasyon ak espesyalis aprantisaj yo”.

strings.text: Longer-term help is by referral: counselors provide “community resource referrals (including longer-term therapy services).”
strings.t: Èd pi long tèm se pa referans: konseye yo bay “referans pou resous nan kominote a (ladan l sèvis terapi pi long tèm)”.

strings.text: A Mental Health and Crisis Resources page lists the Suicide and Crisis Lifeline (“call 988 or text HOME to 741741”) and the NC Peer Warmline; Middle School counselors provide “support to students in crisis.”
strings.t: Yon paj Mental Health and Crisis Resources bay Suicide and Crisis Lifeline (“rele 988 oswa voye HOME pa tèks nan 741741”) ak NC Peer Warmline; konseye Middle School yo bay “sipò pou elèv ki nan kriz”.

strings.text: None named.
strings.t: Pa gen non ki bay.

strings.text: A Lead School Nurse and a School Nurse are listed in the staff directory.
strings.t: Lis estaf la gen yon Lead School Nurse (enfimyè prensipal lekòl) ak yon School Nurse (enfimyè lekòl).

strings.text: International students enroll through an approved placement agency; no English-language support is described.
strings.t: Elèv entènasyonal yo enskri atravè yon ajans plasman ki apwouve; yo pa dekri okenn sipò nan lang angle.

strings.text: Speech therapy is by referral. The school’s site lists no occupational or physical therapy.
strings.t: Terapi lapawòl se pa referans. Sit lekòl la pa mansyone terapi okipasyonèl ni fizyoterapi.

strings.text: The Learning Specialist helps families find an outside speech therapist.
strings.t: Espesyalis aprantisaj la ede fanmi yo jwenn yon terapis lapawòl deyò.

strings.text: No therapist appears in the school’s staff directory. Ask whether an outside therapist can see your child on campus during the school day.
strings.t: Okenn terapis pa parèt nan lis estaf lekòl la. Mande si yon terapis deyò ka wè pitit ou sou kanpis la pandan jounen lekòl la.

strings.text: Cannon doesn’t run diagnostic testing itself. Families bring a recent psychologist’s evaluation, and the school identifies early needs in the classroom.
strings.t: Cannon pa fè tès dyagnostik li menm. Fanmi yo pote yon evalyasyon resan yon sikològ fè, epi lekòl la idantifye bezwen bonè yo nan klas la.

strings.text: A recent psychoeducational evaluation
strings.t: Yon evalyasyon psikoedikasyonèl resan

strings.text: The evaluation must be from “a recent (last 3 years)” period and done “by a licensed clinical psychologist,” with “comprehensive cognitive and academic assessment.”
strings.t: Evalyasyon an dwe soti nan yon peryòd “resan (3 dènye ane yo)” epi fèt “pa yon sikològ klinik ki gen lisans”, ak “yon evalyasyon kognitif ak akademik konplè”.

strings.text: The school does not test in-house or name providers.
strings.t: Lekòl la pa fè tès anndan l, ni li pa nonmen founisè.

strings.text: Classroom identification, JK–2
strings.t: Idantifikasyon nan klas, JK–2

strings.text: The Learning Specialist “collaborates closely with teachers to assess student needs, differentiate instruction, and implement targeted strategies within the classroom.”
strings.t: Espesyalis aprantisaj la “travay kole kole ak pwofesè yo pou evalye bezwen elèv yo, adapte ansèyman an, epi aplike estrateji ki vize nan klas la”.

strings.text: College Board and ACT accommodations
strings.t: Akomodasyon College Board ak ACT

strings.text: For juniors and seniors, “additional guidance is offered to help navigate the process of requesting testing accommodations from the College Board and ACT,” once a Learning Plan has been in place for at least four months.
strings.t: Pou elèv twazyèm ak dènye ane yo, “yo ofri plis konsèy pou ede yo navige pwosesis pou mande akomodasyon pou tès nan College Board ak ACT”, lè yon Learning Plan an plas pou omwen kat mwa.

strings.text: Twelve named staff: four learning specialists and deans, a reading interventionist, two ARC faculty and five school counselors.
strings.t: Douz manm estaf ki gen non: kat espesyalis aprantisaj ak dwayen, yon espesyalis entèvansyon nan lekti, de pwofesè ARC ak senk konseye lekòl.

strings.t: Konseye Lower School, klas JrK - 2

strings.text: Lower & Middle School Counselor, Grades 3 - 5
strings.t: Konseye Lower School ak Middle School, klas 3 - 5

strings.t: Yo pa nonmen yon sèl responsab pou sipò aprantisaj.

strings.t: Tracy Wade dirije Dovi Academic Resource Center Middle School la; Jennifer Ridenhour dirije pa Upper School la.

strings.text: Davidson Day’s Learning Enrichment Center “provides personalized, one-on-one instruction that supports students ages two through grade 12,” with tutoring, academic coaching, social skills groups, and speech and occupational therapy on campus.

strings.text: The Learning Enrichment Center is open to students at every grade, by request. The school publishes no eligibility criteria and does not mention 504 plans or IEPs.
strings.t: Learning Enrichment Center la louvri pou elèv nan tout klas, sou demann. Lekòl la pa pibliye okenn kritè pou kalifye epi li pa mansyone plan 504 ni IEP.

strings.text: Each LEC service is “available to students at all grade levels,” and the center supports “students ages two through grade 12.” Families “submit our request form,” and the Director of Learning Services “will then call you to discuss the kind of academic support your child needs.” The 2026-2027 request form asks for no diagnosis, evaluation or other documentation.
strings.t: Chak sèvis LEC “disponib pou elèv nan tout nivo klas”, epi sant lan sipòte “elèv depi laj dezan rive nan 12yèm ane”. Fanmi yo “soumèt fòmilè demann nou an”, epi direktè sèvis aprantisaj la “ap rele w apre sa pou n pale sou kalite sipò akademik pitit ou bezwen”. Fòmilè demann 2026-2027 la pa mande okenn dyagnostik, evalyasyon oswa lòt dokiman.

strings.text: The school’s pages do not mention 504 plans, IEPs or accommodations, and the LEC request form does not ask about them.
strings.t: Paj lekòl la pa mansyone plan 504, IEP ni akomodasyon, epi fòmilè demann LEC la pa poze kesyon sou yo.

strings.text: The school’s pages do not say what the LEC does not provide. The one stated limit is on coaching: “Academic Coaching is more than ‘homework help’,” and “Students will likely have homework remaining after sessions.”
strings.t: Paj lekòl la pa di sa LEC la pa bay. Sèl limit yo bay la gen pou wè ak coaching: “Academic Coaching se plis pase ‘èd pou devwa’”, epi “Elèv yo ap gen plis chans toujou gen devwa ki rete apre sesyon yo”.

strings.text: Admission asks for “current transcripts and teacher recommendations,” and the school says it “does not discriminate on the basis of” disability, among other categories.
strings.t: Admisyon mande “dosye nòt aktyèl ak rekòmandasyon pwofesè”, epi lekòl la di li “pa fè diskriminasyon sou baz” andikap, pami lòt kategori.

strings.text: Every service the school’s pages describe, grouped and coded by who delivers it. LEC services are billed; the school publishes its summer 2026 rates but not its school-year rates. Pick your child’s need to see what applies.
strings.t: Chak sèvis paj lekòl la dekri, gwoupe epi kode selon kiyès ki bay li. Sèvis LEC yo peye; lekòl la pibliye pri ete 2026 li yo, men li pa pibliye pri ane lekòl la. Chwazi bezwen pitit ou pou w wè sa ki aplike.

strings.text: One-on-one tutoring for reading, plus a Lower School literacy coach and reading specialist. No reading method is named.
strings.t: Titora youn a youn pou lekti, plis yon coach alfabetizasyon ak yon espesyalis lekti nan Lower School. Yo pa nonmen okenn metòd lekti.

strings.text: LEC tutoring can “address specific academic difficulties (reading fluency and comprehension or math skills).” Ask which reading approach the specialists use.
strings.t: Titora LEC ka “trete difikilte akademik espesifik (fliyidite ak konpreyansyon nan lekti oswa konpetans nan matematik)”. Mande ki apwòch lekti espesyalis yo itilize.

strings.text: One-on-one academic coaching for executive function, at every grade.
strings.t: Coaching akademik youn a youn pou fonksyon egzekitif, nan tout klas.

strings.text: Coaching helps students “develop organizational and time management skills, learning techniques, and self-advocacy,” and every Middle School student takes a study skills course each year.
strings.t: Coaching ede elèv yo “devlope konpetans nan òganizasyon ak jesyon tan, teknik aprantisaj, ak defann tèt yo”, epi chak elèv Middle School pran yon kou sou metòd etid chak ane.

strings.text: One-on-one math tutoring, by request.
strings.t: Titora youn a youn nan matematik, sou demann.

strings.text: LEC instructors give “review or remedial instruction” in subjects including Math, and tutoring “is often done during the school day, often during a study hall period.”
strings.t: Enstriktè LEC yo bay “ansèyman revizyon oswa ratrapaj” nan matyè tankou matematik, epi titora a “souvan fèt pandan jounen lekòl la, souvan pandan yon peryòd etid”.

strings.text: On campus during the school day, through a contracted provider.
strings.t: Sou kanpis la pandan jounen lekòl la, atravè yon founisè ki gen kontra.

strings.text: “Davidson Day School has a contract with Speech Techniques to provide speech-language services on campus during the school day,” with sessions “typically lasting 30-minutes.”
strings.t: “Davidson Day School gen yon kontra ak Speech Techniques pou bay sèvis lapawòl-lang sou kanpis la pandan jounen lekòl la”, ak sesyon “ki dire anjeneral 30 minit”.

strings.text: Occupational therapy on campus through a contracted provider. No physical therapy is listed.
strings.t: Terapi okipasyonèl sou kanpis la atravè yon founisè ki gen kontra. Yo pa mete fizyoterapi sou lis la.

strings.text: Integrative Wellness provides OT “on campus during the school day as an additional service,” for “handwriting, visual-motor integration, sensory processing, social skills, and other fine motor skills.”
strings.t: Integrative Wellness bay terapi okipasyonèl “sou kanpis la pandan jounen lekòl la kòm yon sèvis anplis”, pou “ekriti alamen, entegrasyon vizyèl-motè, tretman sansoryèl, konpetans sosyal, ak lòt konpetans motrisite fen”.

strings.text: Social skills groups led by an occupational therapist, and two school counselors.
strings.t: Gwoup konpetans sosyal ke yon terapis okipasyonèl dirije, ak de konseye lekòl.

strings.text: Groups of “3-4 students, grouped by age and goal areas” meet weekly for 30 minutes. The directory lists a Lower School Counselor and a Middle and Upper School Counselor.
strings.t: Gwoup “3-4 elèv, gwoupe selon laj ak objektif” rankontre chak semèn pandan 30 minit. Anyè a gen yon konseye Lower School ak yon konseye Middle School ak Upper School.

strings.text: Upper School courses for ready Middle Schoolers, and an enrichment option in the LEC. No formal gifted program.
strings.t: Kou Upper School pou elèv Middle School ki pare, ak yon opsyon anrichisman nan LEC la. Pa gen pwogram fòmèl pou elèv ki gen don.

strings.text: Middle Schoolers “ready to learn at the next level” can take world language and mathematics in the Upper School, and the LEC request form offers “Personalized Exploration (Enrichment) focused on student's passions and curiosities.”
strings.t: Elèv Middle School ki “pare pou aprann nan nivo pi wo a” ka pran lang etranjè ak matematik nan Upper School, epi fòmilè demann LEC la ofri “Personalized Exploration (Enrichment) ki konsantre sou pasyon ak kiryozite elèv la”.

strings.text: Nine Learning Specialists, a Lower School Literacy Coach and a Director of Learning Services staff the LEC; the directory also lists a Lower School Reading Specialist.
strings.t: Nèf espesyalis aprantisaj, yon coach alfabetizasyon Lower School ak yon direktè sèvis aprantisaj fòme ekip LEC la; anyè a gen yon espesyalis lekti Lower School tou.

strings.text: One-on-one tutoring can “address specific academic difficulties (reading fluency and comprehension or math skills).” No method (e.g., Orton-Gillingham, structured literacy) is named.
strings.t: Titora youn a youn ka “trete difikilte akademik espesifik (fliyidite ak konpreyansyon nan lekti oswa konpetans nan matematik)”. Yo pa nonmen okenn metòd (pa egzanp, Orton-Gillingham, alfabetizasyon estriktire).

strings.text: One-on-one tutoring in “math skills,” as part of LEC tutoring.
strings.t: Titora youn a youn nan “konpetans matematik”, kòm yon pati nan titora LEC.

strings.text: LEC instructors “meet with students in a one-on-one setting for one or more sessions per week.” The only small groups are the social skills groups, of “3-4 students.”
strings.t: Enstriktè LEC yo “rankontre elèv yo youn a youn pou youn oswa plizyè sesyon chak semèn”. Sèl ti gwoup yo se gwoup konpetans sosyal yo, ak “3-4 elèv”.

strings.text: Subject tutoring
strings.t: Titora pa matyè

strings.text: Sessions provide “review or remedial instruction in a specific subject area (Language Arts, Math, Science, Social Studies, and/or Foreign Language),” often “during a study hall period.”
strings.t: Sesyon yo bay “ansèyman revizyon oswa ratrapaj nan yon matyè espesifik (Language Arts, Math, Science, Social Studies, ak/oswa Foreign Language)”, souvan “pandan yon peryòd etid”.

strings.text: Academic coaching builds “organizational and time management skills, learning techniques, and self-advocacy.” It “is more than ‘homework help’.”
strings.t: Coaching akademik bati “konpetans nan òganizasyon ak jesyon tan, teknik aprantisaj, ak defann tèt yo”. Li “se plis pase ‘èd pou devwa’”.

strings.text: No learning-support class is described, but “every Middle School student takes a study skills course each year.”
strings.t: Yo pa dekri okenn kou sipò aprantisaj, men “chak elèv Middle School pran yon kou sou metòd etid chak ane”.

strings.text: Not described. The LEC’s learning specialists “will have direct contact with the classroom teacher,” and families get a weekly email.
strings.t: Yo pa dekri l. Espesyalis aprantisaj LEC yo “ap gen kontak dirèk ak pwofesè klas la”, epi fanmi yo resevwa yon imèl chak semèn.

strings.text: Not described. LEC lesson plans are individualized tutoring, not a modified curriculum.
strings.t: Yo pa dekri l. Plan leson LEC yo se titora endividyalize, se pa yon kourikoulòm modifye.

strings.text: Middle Schoolers can take Upper School world language and math; the LEC request form offers “Personalized Exploration (Enrichment).” No formal gifted program.
strings.t: Elèv Middle School ka pran lang etranjè ak matematik Upper School; fòmilè demann LEC la ofri “Personalized Exploration (Enrichment)”. Pa gen pwogram fòmèl pou elèv ki gen don.

strings.text: None asked. The LEC request form asks for grade, services, goals and frequency; admission asks for “current transcripts and teacher recommendations.”
strings.t: Yo pa mande okenn. Fòmilè demann LEC la mande klas, sèvis, objektif ak frekans; admisyon mande “dosye nòt aktyèl ak rekòmandasyon pwofesè”.

strings.text: June 1 to July 30, 2026: tutoring $47 for 30 minutes, $63 for 40 and $78 for 50; occupational therapy $160 for a 60-minute session; speech therapy $80 for a 30-minute session, all “billed directly to your Patriot Account.”
strings.t: Soti 1ye jen rive 30 jiyè 2026: titora $47 pou 30 minit, $63 pou 40 ak $78 pou 50; terapi okipasyonèl $160 pou yon sesyon 60 minit; terapi lapawòl $80 pou yon sesyon 30 minit, tout “yo mete l dirèkteman sou Patriot Account ou”.

strings.text: Through a contract with Speech Techniques, “on campus during the school day,” one-on-one, with sessions “typically lasting 30-minutes.”
strings.t: Atravè yon kontra ak Speech Techniques, “sou kanpis la pandan jounen lekòl la”, youn a youn, ak sesyon “ki dire anjeneral 30 minit”.

strings.text: Through a contract with Integrative Wellness, “on campus during the school day as an additional service,” one-on-one.
strings.t: Atravè yon kontra ak Integrative Wellness, “sou kanpis la pandan jounen lekòl la kòm yon sèvis anplis”, youn a youn.

strings.text: No screening is described. The Gesell Readiness Assessment is an admission test.
strings.t: Yo pa dekri okenn depistaj. Gesell Readiness Assessment se yon tès admisyon.

strings.text: Not described, for the ISEE or school exams.
strings.t: Yo pa dekri yo, ni pou ISEE ni pou egzamen lekòl yo.

strings.text: The Gesell Readiness Assessment (Junior Kindergarten–1st Grade), a reading assessment plus the at-home ISEE (2nd–4th Grade), and the ISEE (5th–12th Grade).
strings.t: Gesell Readiness Assessment (Junior Kindergarten rive 1ye ane), yon evalyasyon lekti plis ISEE lakay (2yèm rive 4yèm ane), ak ISEE (5yèm rive 12yèm ane).

strings.t: Anyè a gen yon konseye Lower School ak yon konseye Middle School ak Upper School; “Aprantisaj sosyal-emosyonèl se yon poto mitan nan eksperyans Lower School Davidson Day”.

strings.text: Not described beyond the social skills groups.

strings.t: Speech Techniques, sou kanpis la; sesyon anjeneral 30 minit. Ete 2026: $80 pou chak sesyon.

strings.t: Terapis lapawòl-lang lan sou lis anplwaye LEC la. Pri terapi pou ane lekòl la, yo bay fanmi yo li anvan lekòl louvri, epi yo pa pibliye yo.

strings.text: Davidson Day publishes no screening or evaluation for learning differences. A family asks for LEC support with a request form, and the Director of Learning Services follows up by phone.
strings.t: Davidson Day pa pibliye okenn depistaj ni evalyasyon pou diferans nan aprantisaj. Yon fanmi mande sipò LEC ak yon fòmilè demann, epi direktè sèvis aprantisaj la swiv sa nan telefòn.

strings.text: The 2026-2027 request form asks for no diagnosis, evaluation or other documentation.

strings.text: The school does not describe any early identification or screening.

strings.text: Eleven questions to take on the tour, covering what the school’s site leaves unanswered: rates, prior plans, accommodations, methods, evaluation, therapy and staff.
strings.t: Onz kesyon pou pote pandan vizit la, sou sa sit lekòl la kite san repons: pri, plan anvan yo, akomodasyon, metòd, evalyasyon, terapi ak anplwaye.

strings.text: What are the 2026-27 rates for tutoring, academic coaching, social skills groups, speech and occupational therapy, and does financial aid cover any of them?
strings.t: Ki pri 2026-27 yo pou titora, coaching akademik, gwoup konpetans sosyal, terapi lapawòl ak terapi okipasyonèl, epi èske èd finansye kouvri nenpòt nan yo?

strings.text: How is a 504 plan, IEP or prior school’s accommodations plan handled when a student enrolls?
strings.t: Kijan yo jere yon plan 504, yon IEP oswa plan akomodasyon yon ansyen lekòl lè yon elèv enskri?

strings.text: Which classroom and testing accommodations do you provide, and do they apply to the ISEE and to school exams?
strings.t: Ki akomodasyon nan klas ak pou tès nou bay, epi èske yo aplike pou ISEE ak pou egzamen lekòl yo?

strings.text: Which reading method do the Literacy Coach, Reading Specialist and Learning Specialists use (e.g., Orton-Gillingham, Wilson, structured literacy)?
strings.t: Ki metòd lekti coach alfabetizasyon an, espesyalis lekti a ak espesyalis aprantisaj yo itilize (pa egzanp, Orton-Gillingham, Wilson, alfabetizasyon estriktire)?

strings.text: Do you ever modify the curriculum, or is LEC support always tutoring alongside it?
strings.t: Èske nou janm modifye kourikoulòm nan, oswa èske sipò LEC la toujou se titora akote l?

strings.text: Is there any screening for reading, math or attention, and who carries out psychoeducational evaluations? Do you keep a list of evaluators?
strings.t: Èske gen depistaj nan lekti, matematik oswa atansyon, epi kiyès ki fè evalyasyon psikoedikasyonèl yo? Èske nou gen yon lis evalyatè?

strings.text: Is there a school psychologist, and what is the crisis protocol?
strings.t: Èske gen yon sikològ lekòl, epi ki pwotokòl pou kriz?

strings.text: Is physical therapy available on campus?
strings.t: Èske gen fizyoterapi disponib sou kanpis la?

strings.text: Do Speech Techniques and Integrative Wellness bill families through the Patriot Account or directly, and can therapy be billed to insurance?
strings.t: Èske Speech Techniques ak Integrative Wellness fè fanmi yo peye atravè Patriot Account la oswa dirèkteman, epi èske yo ka voye fakti terapi a bay asirans?

strings.text: Is Dr. LaRusso the Director of Learning Services or the Director of Curriculum, and who oversees the LEC?
strings.t: Èske Dr. LaRusso se direktè sèvis aprantisaj oswa direktè kourikoulòm, epi kiyès ki sipèvize LEC la?

strings.text: Educational Support Services (ESS) is the umbrella under which students receive individualized academic supports: academic coaching, tutoring, learning accommodations and specialized support for students with identified learning differences.
strings.t: Educational Support Services (ESS) se kad kote elèv yo resevwa sipò akademik ki fèt pou chak moun: coaching akademik, leson patikilye, aranjman pou aprantisaj, ak sipò espesyalize pou elèv ki gen diferans nan fason yo aprann ki idantifye.

strings.text: Every service is fee-based under an annual contract.
strings.t: Chak sèvis se ak frè, avèk yon kontra chak ane.

strings.text: served by ESS
strings.t: ESS sèvi

strings.text: K through 12th grade, per the 2026–27 fee schedule; ESS access for Transitional Kindergarten is not stated
strings.t: depi K rive nan 12yèm ane, dapre lis frè 2026–27 la; yo pa di si elèv Transitional Kindergarten yo gen aksè a ESS
